newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: LOWER S.AFRICAN SHORTAGE SPAWNS TALK OF RATE CUT.
newsitem.headline: LOWER S.AFRICAN SHORTAGE SPAWNS TALK OF RATE CUT.

text.p: South Africa's money market shortage has moved back below the nine billion rand mark, nudging short-term rates lower and spawning speculation of an early interest rate cut.
Reserve Bank data released on Wednesday showed the shortage eased to 8.937 billion rand on Tuesday -- its lowest level since January 9.
The figure surprised money market traders who are accustomed to month-end pressures traditionally bringing upward pressure to bear on the shortage.
Roelf du Plooy, the Reserve Bank's assistant general manager of money and capital markets, said the lower shortage was primarily a result of foreign exchange flows.
"At the moment (commercial) banks are selling dollars back to the Reserve Bank...in quantities much larger than we expected them to," du Plooy said.

"It is plain forex flows that is causing the shortage to come down," he said, adding that the sale of dollars had outweighed the rise in notes and coins, a major factor which influences the level of the shortage.
Notes and coins in circulation rose over 400 million rand to 19.442 billion rand on Tuesday from 18.997 billion rand on Monday.
The easing in liquidity gave short-term rates their cue to move lower.
Three-month NCD rates were quoted at between 17.05 percent offered and 17.20 percent bid on Wednesday from between 17.10 and 17.25 percent on Tuesday.

"There are a few things that have pushed rates lower," a senior trader said, citing the easing of seasonal December pressures, bullish money supply and credit extension data on Tuesday and the lower shortage.
"We are seeing quality broad-based buying," he said.

Growth in credit extension to the private sector in December was 15.75 percent -- well below market forecasts of a 16.3 percent -- while money supply growth rose 13.73 percent year-on-year against forecasts of 14.3 percent.
Dealers said that while the market had not yet begun to discount an interest rate hike, speculation was beginning to surface.
"It's still too early because the rates are only still in line with where the Bank rate is," a dealer said. Bank rate, the official lending rate, is currently 17 percent.
"The market is starting to settle down and it is not starting to anticipate a rate cut yet but it is getting into that mood."
On the currency market, forward rates also eased in line with the money market, a move which dealers said signalled the market was beginning to discount an interest rate cut.
"We are seeing rand interest rates come off and the money market shortage is also coming off," said Standard Bank forward trader Glen Thompson.
"The (forward) market has just played catch up to the money market and now it is starting to discount a cut in interest rates," Thompson said.
Three-month forward points were at around 12.05 from 12.20 on Tuesday, while one-year points were quoted at 45.15 -- both at their lowest levels since mid-October.
Forward traders said that at current levels, the forward market was discounting an interest rate cut within the next four months.
Economists expect interest rates to be reduced by up to three percentage points this year as credit is brought under control in a slowing economy.
